children.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers

detail.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers
detail.summary: Record robustness is not merely a static property of environmental state redundancy but depends dynamically on system preparation, local field conditions, and the observer's information structure. External observers rely on relativistic causality, whereas internal observers utilize local observables super-algebras, requiring a self-consistency principle to maintain agreement.
detail.reason: Revision incorporates new evidence regarding interaction parameters (peer-4ffc99a8d2e2a1db3830e714) and observer frameworks (source-de600b275ba74792) to address the limitations of the prior notebook.

detail.title: Quantum Scrambling and the Emergence of Objective Records
detail.summary: Scrambling distributes quantum information globally, but environmental interaction parameters and conditional branch separations govern whether reliable redundant records emerge.
detail.reason: Revising notebook findings based on newly collected peer evidence distinguishing scrambling from redundant environmental encoding.
